newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Moslems, Croats reach accord on joint army.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Moslems, Croats reach accord on joint army.

text.p: Bosnia's Croats and Moslems, former enemies turned federal partners, have taken the final steps to form a joint army after a long-stalled process, a U.S. envoy said on Wednesday.

Ambassador James Pardew, charged by the White House with overseeing a U.S.-backed military programme for the federation, said senior Moslem and Croat officials had signed orders for the appointment of the commander and joint command of the federal army.
"The agreement constitutes final approval of these (military) organisations and now allows critical appointments to be made," Pardew told reporters in Sarajevo.
Under the accord, the commander of the Moslem-led Bosnian army, General Rasim Delic, becomes head of the joint command. Croat General Zivko Budimir will be the chief-of-staff.

The orders were signed by Alija Izetbegovic, Moslem leader of Bosnia's collective presidency, and Kresimir Zubak, Croat president of the Croat-Moslem federation which comprises half of Bosnia. The rest is controlled by the Serb republic.

Croats and Moslems waged war in 1993-94 before bowing to U.S. pressure and forming the federation. But the deal has never moved much beyond agreements on paper because of narrow nationalist agendas and mistrust on both sides.
